title: Remove maintenance WebView flat exports
summary: Removed the seven maintenanceView direct flat window exports and migrated app, app/home, app/lifecycle, and diagnostics consumers to window.mediaPipelineMaintenanceView. Refreshed the WebView public contract baseline, global export inventory, and generated summaries.
reason: Continue namespace-first WebView cleanup by reducing transitional flat exports in the touched Maintenance domain without changing backend-owned maintenance command routes or payloads.
behavior_before: maintenanceView.js exposed hasMaintenanceLoaded, getLastMaintenance, refreshMaintenance, initMaintenanceViewEvents, runReleaseDryRun, runReleaseBuild, and runBackfillDryRun directly on window, and app-level consumers called those flat helpers.
behavior_after: Maintenance helpers are exposed through mediaPipelineMaintenanceView only; app-level, Home, lifecycle, and Diagnostics consumers use the namespace while backend maintenance command ownership remains unchanged.
manual_validation: python -m unittest tests.webview.test_webview_browser_diagnostics_handoff_smoke -q - passed; fixture emitted broken ActiveJobs record warnings but tests passed
validate_changes --require-worktree-coverage - passed after packet field update
rollback_plan: Restore the seven window.<maintenance helper> assignments in maintenanceView.js, revert app/Home/lifecycle/Diagnostics consumers to the prior flat helper calls if needed, regenerate the WebView public contract/inventory, refresh summaries, and rerun the same WebView static and maintenance/Home/Diagnostics browser checks.
notes:
Removed maintenanceView flat aliases and migrated app/diagnostics consumers to mediaPipelineMaintenanceView.
Updated WebView public contract and global export inventory for maintenance flat export removal.
Refreshed generated summaries for maintenance namespace cleanup.
